heroHeadline: Trump Signals 'Decisive Decision' on Iran, Warns of Imminent Escalation
heroSubtitle: Day 199 (September 13, 2026): A cluster of setbacks for Hormuz diplomacy and Gulf security. On Sept 9 (Day 195), CSIS satellite analysis found a construction surge at Iran's suspected underground Pickaxe Mountain nuclear site near Natanz, as the US maintains strike plans for reaching it. On Sept 10 (Day 196), long-range drones launched from Iraq's Maysan province struck Saudi Arabia's East-West pipeline — the kingdom's main alternative to the Strait of Hormuz — forcing a shutdown; Brent crude spiked to $109.20/bbl intraday, a four-month high. Iraq dismissed the responsible commander and closed border crossings with Iran. On Sept 11 (Day 197), Iran announced it would meet Gulf states and Iraq in Oman on Sept 14 for the first such gathering since the war began, but on Sept 12 (Day 198) Bahrain refused to join, citing its severed diplomatic ties with Tehran since 2016; separately, 3 Iranian security personnel were killed in a clash with gunmen in Saravan. On Sept 13 (Day 199), Iraq seized the drone-launching platform used in the pipeline attack, an Iranian commercial vessel was struck by an unidentified projectile near Hengam Island (1 killed, 4 wounded), and a New York Times report — cited by regional outlets — described hardliners around cleric Hossein Taeb staging unauthorized July Hormuz attacks that derailed a near-complete US-Iran peace deal without President Pezeshkian's knowledge. Brent crude eased to ~$104/bbl on the Oman-talks announcement even as the pipeline and vessel strikes underscored the fragility of the corridor.
